scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: dividing by zero
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We divide ten by zero. Python says, zero division error, division by zero. Maths has no answer, so Python stops. In the calculator, a user can type any numbers, so we must guard. Check that the divisor is not zero, and print a friendly message otherwise.

shorts.title: Calculator plan
shorts.script: Let us build a calculator. One function, calculate, takes two numbers and an operator, and returns the answer. A loop asks the user for a line like six star seven, until they type q. We split the line, convert the numbers, call the function, and print the result. Small pieces that each do one job, working together. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Our functions project.

shorts.title: One job per function
shorts.script: Keep the calculate function pure. It takes values in, and returns a value out. It does not ask for input, and it does not print. That makes it easy to test, and easy to reuse. The loop handles the talking to the user. Calculate only does maths. Separate the jobs, and your programs stay clear as they grow. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Keep functions focused.

shorts.title: A dictionary of functions
shorts.hook: "A long if and elif ladder can become a dictionary."
shorts.script: A long if and elif ladder can become a dictionary. Each key is an operator, and each value is a lambda that does the job. Ops, bracket plus, close bracket, open bracket, two, three, close bracket, gives five. Adding a new operator means adding one line. Functions are values, so a dictionary can hold them, like anything else. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Functions in a dictionary.

shorts.title: Zero division
shorts.script: Every calculator needs this guard. Ten divided by zero has no answer. Python raises a zero division error, division by zero, and your program stops. The user typed the numbers, so you must expect zero. Check that the divisor is not zero, before you divide. Print a friendly message instead. Defensive code keeps programs running. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Guard the divisor.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the calculator go to the beach?"
shorts.script: Why did the calculator go to the beach? It wanted to add some sun. Your challenge. Add a new operator to the calculator, double star, which raises the first number to the power of the second. Test it with two double star eight. You should see two fifty six point zero. Remember to add a new branch to the ladder. Share your code below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 50.
